verses.t: And when they came to Tulanzú (the seven caves and seven ravines), the ancient traditions say, they had walked far to reach Tulanzú, and they had no fire. But they stayed where the god Tohil was, who was the god of the people who first created fire; and it is not known how he created it, but the fire was already shining. When Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam saw it, they exclaimed, "Ah, lord, we have none of this fire that has been made, and we shall die of cold!" And then the god spoke and said, "Do not grieve; you have something of your own. That fire you speak of will come to an end and be lost." "Can it be so?" they said, rejoicing. "God, you are our sustenance and our food, you, god!" And then they gave him thanks for what he had said, and he said, "Very well. Truly I am your god when it dawns, and I shall be your lord." This was said to the chiefs by Tohil; and so the peoples warmed themselves and rejoiced over the fire.

And then a great downpour began, while the fire of the peoples was burning, and much hail fell on all of them; and then their fire was put out by the hail, and they had no fire any more. And then Balam-quitzé and Balam-acab asked for their fire again: "Ah, god, we are perishing of cold," they said to Tohil. "Very well," he said, "do not grieve." And then he drew out fire by twisting it in his sandal; and then Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam rejoiced, and then they warmed themselves. And the fire of the peoples having gone out, they were dying of cold, and they came to ask Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam for fire. And they could no longer bear the cold and the frost, but were shivering, their teeth chattering, and they were like dead men, their feet and hands bent and crippled, and they could hold nothing with them when they came. "We are not ashamed before you to ask you for fire; give us a little of your fire!" they said when they arrived. But no answer was given them, and then the peoples grew angry. The language of Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam was different, and the peoples said, "What is this? These have abandoned our language. How did this happen? Are we lost? Where were we deceived? For our language was one when we came from Tulanzú, and our origin and upbringing were one. What we have done is not good," said all the peoples, beneath the trees and vines. And then a man appeared (a demon who spoke to them) before Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam; and the messenger of the underworld spoke and said, "This truly is your god, and this is the one who sustains you, and this is the substitute and replacement, the remembrance of your Creator and Former. Do not give his fire to the peoples until you ask Tohil, and he will tell you whether you shall give it or not." So said that one from the underworld, who had wings like a bat; and he said, "I am the messenger of your Creator and Former." And the heart of Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz rejoiced and was exalted when the messenger said this; and then he vanished from before them. And then the peoples arrived without delay, and they were perishing of cold, for because of the much hail and the continual drizzle the cold was unbearable; and all the peoples arrived stiff and shivering with cold when they came to where Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were; and they were grieving, rubbing their faces and their mouths.

And afterwards the thieves came to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam and said to them, "Have you no pity on us, who ask for a little fire? We come from one and the same house, and we all come from one and the same homeland, from when you were formed and created. Have mercy on us." And they said, "What will you give us, so that we may have mercy on you?" And the peoples said to them, "Good; we shall give you silver." And the four said to the peoples, "We do not want silver." "Then we shall ask for what you want." "Very well," said the peoples, of Dildo (?), to Tohil. "We shall let you know afterwards," they said to the peoples. And then they asked Tohil, "What shall we give the peoples, who come to ask for fire?" said Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam. "Very well," said Tohil. "If they will join themselves to me, if they will give their side and their tobacco, and if they wish it, I shall take them under my care and I shall be their Tohil; and if they do not wish it, I shall not give them their fire," said Tohil. "And tell them that little by little, and not now, they must give us their sides and their tobacco. Tell them this," it was said to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam. And then they told what Tohil had said. "Very well," said the peoples, "it shall be joined, and we shall obey him," they said, answering what Tohil had said. And they did not delay, but said, "Very well, let it be done at once." And then they received their fire, and then they warmed themselves.
